key_insight: Iterative strong coupling stabilizes FD-SPH simulations of lightweight floating rigid bodies where single-pass coupling fails, even with much smaller time steps.
engineering_relevance: The method supports simulation of lightweight, complex-shaped floating bodies in transient free-surface flows without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation.
method: Couple volume-based FD-SPH hydrodynamic loads with Newton–Euler rigid-body updates.
Iteratively feed back the velocity mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious fluid and the rigid body within each time step.
Analyze when Passively Moving Solid projection and Newton–Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities.
evidence_signal: Settling-disk and dam-break tests agree with published results or experimental trends; cube tests remain stable at specific gravities of 0.1–1.0 with iterative coupling, while single-pass coupling fails at 0.1 and 0.2.
watch_item: Strong coupling requires a residual-controlled iteration loop; all reported production runs converged, but computational overhead is not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
